items.summary: An unauthenticated remote attacker can perform password resets for any user with known username and email without rate limiting. This can result in a total loss of availabilit since the password will be reseted.
A high privileged remote attacker can upload arbitrary files to a guessable location. This can result in a loss of availability and might be chained with other vulnerabilities.
The backups created by the application use a weak static password allowing an unauthenticated remote attacker to access their content. This can result in a total loss of confidentiality.

An unauthenticated remote attacker can perform a XSS attack on a logged in backend user allowing for execution of multiple critical system actions. This could allow an attacker to shutdown the server or restore an uploaded backup. This can result in a loss of integrity and availability.

An unauthenticated remote attacker can perform an authentication bypass on the com_check function, potentially triggering traffic on other systems and email alerts. This can result in some loss of availability due to higher system loads.

An unauthenticated remote attacker can perform a CSRF attack on a logged in backend user allowing for execution of multiple critical system actions. This could allow an attacker to shutdown the server or restore an uploaded backup. This can result in a loss of integrity and availability.
